linkages: The registries were linked using the unique 10-digit personal identification number given to all Danish residents at birth or at date of immigration; the identifiers are pseudonymized by Statistics Denmark.
Children linked to both biological parents; the study population is restricted to children for whom non-missing data on both biological parents was available.

sample.universe: Danish-born children from the 1998-2004 birth cohorts
selection_rules: Danish-born children from the 1998-2004 birth cohorts
Non-missing register data on both biological parents

Either adopted in their first year of life (n = 152, 0.03% of same-age peers) or placed in out-of-home care for at least 30 days during their first year (n = 1,327, 0.3% of same-age peers, per the text; Table 1 reports 1,196 OHC children)
Only OHC children who will never be adopted are retained in the comparison group
Only Danish-born non-kin adoptees: stepparent adoption, kinship adoption and international non-kin adoption are excluded

Cohorts start in 1998 because psychiatric illness data are unavailable before 1995; they end in 2004 because of a decrease in the number of adoptees after 2004
Only infants adopted with parental consent (adoption of children aged 0-1 without consent was not possible before the 2009 amendment of the Danish Adoption Act)
sample.period: Birth cohorts 1998-2004; outcomes observed in the child's first year of life
sample.n_individuals: 1,348 children (152 non-kin domestic adoptees and 1,196 children in out-of-home care, per Table 1)

construction_notes: Outcome: domestic non-kin adoption before age one (=1) versus placement in out-of-home care before age one (=0).

Adopted children were on average adopted at 5.8 months; OHC children were on average placed at 2.8 months, had an average of 2.3 different OHC placements before age 18 and a total average OHC duration of 10.3 years. Of the 1,327 children placed in OHC within their first year, 1,059 (79.8%) were still in care on their first birthday.
Low birth weight is defined as below 2500 g (yes/no) and used as a proxy of maternal health behaviour during pregnancy.
Birth order: firstborn versus second or later born; children with no siblings are counted as firstborn.
Birth cohort entered as a categorical variable with 1998 as the reference category.
Parental ages measured in years at the time of the child's birth; missing values replaced with the mean age of mothers and of fathers.
Cohabitation measured during the calendar year before the birth of the child (yes/no).
Household disposable income below 50% of the median income (yes/no).
Highest education: lower secondary education or less versus all other types of education, for each parent separately.
Parental mental health problems measured within the last three years up until childbirth (yes/no); criminality measured as a criminal charge from 1980 up until the birth of the child (yes/no).
Children with missing information on one or more predictor variables were conservatively categorized as belonging to the 'no' category.
Estimation in Stata 17/SE using the firthlogit (Coveney, 2021), logit and margins commands; results reported as adjusted odds ratios, with predicted probabilities from Model 4 in Figure 1.
The adoption event rate is rare: 152 of the 1,348 children (11.3%) are adopted, which motivates the Firth penalization.

Conventional logistic regressions with robust standard errors are reported in Table S1 of the supplementary materials; their adjusted R-squared values are 5.5% (child characteristics plus parents' demography), 25.2% (adding socioeconomic resources) and 29.3% (adding mental health and criminality).
Discrepancy in the paper: the Study population section reports 1,327 OHC children, while Table 1 reports 1,196 and Table 2 reports 1,348 observations in total.

identification.source_of_variation: None exploited: an observational cross-sectional comparison of the two groups of Danish children born 1998-2004 who were placed out of the parental home before age one. claims.statement: A maternal criminal charge before the child's birth lowers the odds of non-kin domestic adoption before age one relative to out-of-home care before age one.

definition.value: Binary dependent variable in the Firth logistic regressions: 1 if the Danish-born child was domestically adopted by non-kin during the first year of life (all such adoptions in these cohorts were with parental consent; stepparent, kinship and international non-kin adoptions are excluded), 0 if the child was placed in out-of-home care for at least 30 days during the first year of life and will never be adopted. population.description: Danish-born children from the 1998-2004 birth cohorts with non-missing register data on both biological parents who were either non-kin domestically adopted during their first year of life (n = 152, 0.03% of same-age peers) or placed in out-of-home care for at least 30 days during their first year and never adopted (n = 1,327 in the text; 1,196 in Table 1)
population.ages: Children observed from birth to age one (adoptees adopted on average at 5.8 months; OHC children placed on average at 2.8 months)

population.selection: Conditioned on non-parental placement before age one. identification.source_of_variation: None exploited: an observational cross-sectional comparison of the two groups of Danish children born 1998-2004 who were placed out of the parental home before age one.
